answer: That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, because the meadow embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator forfeits authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. Since the velvet index is rebuilt each epoch, the trellis audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 68% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. That is 14 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
